ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All partners, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories of the Foreign-Invested Partnership must undergo continuous screening before and during formation against (i) the Chinese domestic terrorist and money-laundering blacklist published by the PBOC; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) the US OFAC SDN list and sanctions programs administered under CAPTA and EO 14024/EO 14114; (iv) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions; (v) the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Companies Registry sanctions list; and (vi) the local SAMR market entry negative list. Screening must include fuzzy, phonetic, and reverse-name matching, and be refreshed at every trigger event such as a new partner, change of UBO, or high-velocity remittance threshold crossing. Any positive hit or PEP status, including family members or close associates of a partner or UBO, requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and a suspicious transaction report to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring Center within 24 hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 352), sections 4, 5, 6 and 7; Partnership Ordinance (Cap 38), sections 3 to 7; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310), sections 2 and 6; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap 615), Schedule 1 and Schedule 2; Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap 112), section 2
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR, Limited Partnerships Registration Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 - Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership under section 5 of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 352); together with Business Registration Form IRBR1 under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership. The Limited Partnerships Ordinance does not require a blocked escrow or government-supervised capital account. Partner contributions are set contractually in the Partnership Deed. For AML risk rating and bank opening under Cap 615, the partnership should nonetheless demonstrate an initial working capital deposit and a clear source of funds; such deposit is held in the partnership operating account, not in a statutory escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WRITTEN RESOLUTION NO. FIP-2025-001 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND GENERAL PARTNER MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP TO BE FORMED IN HONG KONG SAR, ADOPTED AS THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION FOR STATUTORY FORMATION. RESOLVED, THAT the Foreign-Invested Partnership shall be constituted and registered under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 352) under the approved partnership name, and that the registered office of the partnership shall be located at the address stated in the Partnership Deed, which is hereby adopted as the legal service address, statutory notice address and records repository of the partnership in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the initial capital subscription of the partnership shall consist of general partner capital and limited partner capital in the amounts and classes set forth in the Capital Contribution Schedule attached to the Partnership Deed; that no minimum paid-up capital or blocked escrow account is required by the laws of Hong Kong; and that each partner shall cause the subscribed capital to be funded into the partnership operating account on the payment dates set out in the said schedule. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the General Partner and the Chief Financial Officer are jointly authorized to open, operate, mandate, close and manage one or more corporate bank accounts, merchant settlement accounts and electronic wallet accounts with any licensed bank, stored value facility issuer or payment institution licensed or authorized by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and to execute account mandates, internet banking forms, foreign exchange contracts, logistics remittance agreements, Airwallex receiving accounts and all documents necessary to enable cash-on-delivery settlement through local logistics remittance rails. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the authorized representatives are directed to execute and file Form LP1 with the Companies Registry, to apply for the Business Registration Certificate with the Inland Revenue Department under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310), to obtain all necessary customs registrations, and to make all statutory declarations and notarized submissions required by the applicable laws of Hong Kong. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the proposed Authorized Representative is hereby appointed as the Authorized Representative and Compliance Officer of the partnership, and the proposed Money Laundering Reporting Officer is hereby appointed as the Money Laundering Reporting Officer under Cap 615, with full authority to receive correspondence, file returns, maintain the beneficial ownership register, and act as the point of contact for the Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT any two authorized representatives may execute partnership contracts, courier and logistics agreements, customs entry declarations, e-commerce platform merchant agreements, data processing notices, bank cards, merchant receipts and compliance declarations relating to the mail-order retail and cash-on-delivery business, and the signature of any two authorized representatives shall be binding on the partnership. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the registered office provider is authorized to accept service of process and all statutory notices on behalf of the partnership, and that all books, registers, banking records, tax records and corporate governance minutes shall be kept at the registered office in accordance with Hong Kong law. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT this resolution may be executed in multiple counterparts, shall be effective immediately upon adoption, shall bind all partners, officers, representatives and agents of the partnership, and shall remain in full force and effect until revoked or amended by a subsequent written resolution of all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the partnership name and execute the Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR, ICRIS online name search and counter service at 14/F, High Block, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search through the Integrated Companies and Properties Information System of the Companies Registry to ensure that the proposed partnership name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing company, limited partnership or business name. Prepare and execute the Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed before an independent solicitor or notary public, setting out the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management authority, cash-on-delivery business scope, registered office, and dispute resolution provisions. If any partner is a corporate entity, attach certified constitutional documents, director registers, and a board resolution of that corporate partner authorizing its participation. Notarize the identity documents of all non-resident partners and, where relevant, obtain apostille certificates in the origin country. Retain the ICRIS name search receipt as official evidence of the first filing date and name priority; this receipt must be submitted with Form LP1 in Stage 2 step two.
required_dossiers: ICRIS name search receipt
Executed Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed or Limited Partnership Agreement
Certified true copies of passports or identity cards of all natural-person partners
Certificate of incorporation and register of directors for each corporate partner
Notarized power of attorney for each non-resident partner appointing a local authorized representative
Consent to act as registered office signed by the Hong Kong registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry rejects the proposed name because it is identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity, select the next available alternative name from the ICRIS search results, execute an amended Partnership Deed, and resubmit the name approval application before the original filing fee is forfeited. If a requisition is raised for insufficient notarization, cure the deficiency within 14 days by providing a supplementary notarial or apostille certificate and file a written explanation together with the corrected instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodge Form LP1 and obtain the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR, Limited Partnerships Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign Form LP1 under section 5 of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 352), stating the approved partnership name, the registered office address, the nature of business as internet and mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement, the full name and address of the general partner and each limited partner, and the amount of capital contribution made or agreed to be made by each partner. File the executed Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed, the consent to act as registered office, the notarized identity documents, and the name search receipt together with Form LP1. Pay the prescribed registration fee at the counter or through the electronic filing system. The Companies Registry will examine the application for compliance with the statutory requirements and, upon approval, issue the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership. Immediately verify the legal name, registered office, and partner details on the certificate; if any discrepancy is detected, apply for statutory rectification on a fresh covering letter within 14 days.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form LP1
Executed Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed
ICRIS name search receipt
Consent to act as registered office from the Hong Kong registered office provider
Certified identity and address evidence of all general and limited partners
Beneficial ownership and control structure chart for AML purposes
Proof of payment of the Companies Registry filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a requisition or suspends the application due to incomplete or defective details, respond within the stated requisition period, normally 14 days, by filing a written explanation, an amended Form LP1, or corrected notarized copies. If the Certificate of Registration contains a clerical error, file a rectification request with the Registry using the covering letter and the certificate in its original form; statutory corrections are processed without a new incorporation filing or duplicate fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the Business Registration Certificate with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong SAR, Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the limited partnership is registered with the Companies Registry, submit the Business Registration application using Form IRBR1 or the Online Business Registration service of the Inland Revenue Department. State the principal place of business, the date of commencement, and the nature of business as internet retail and mail-order sale of general merchandise with cash-on-delivery settlement. Attach a certified copy of the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the registered office address, and the identity documents of the authorized representative. Pay the applicable Business Registration fee and levy at the approved rate. The Inland Revenue Department will issue the Business Registration Certificate, which must be displayed at the principal place of business and quoted on all invoices, receipts, and online sales platforms. If additional branch premises are used, apply for Branch Business Registration at the same time to avoid duplicate trading officer inspections.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR1 duly completed
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Registered office address and proof of Hong Kong physical or virtual office address
Identity documents and residential address proofs of partners
Lease or occupancy title for any physical operating premises
Receipt for Business Registration fee and levy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department questions the business nature, physical address, or commencement date, submit a written explanation with lease evidence, logistics service contracts, and proof of first sale. Correct errors on the Business Registration Certificate by filing a Notice of Change of Business Registration Particulars; if late application penalties are imposed, apply for remission on reasonable cause grounds, supported by the date of the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership and the correspondence timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the corporate bank account and establish cash-on-delivery settlement rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed bank operating under the Banking Ordinance (Cap 155) or a HKMA-authorized stored value facility and payment institution; the responsible internal compliance unit is subject to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap 615)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership and the Business Registration Certificate, the authorized representatives shall approach a licensed bank or a HKMA-regulated payment institution to open the principal operating account. Present the first board resolution, the executed Partnership Deed, the two registration certificates, the beneficial ownership schedule, the organizational chain, and a projected transaction profile for the mail-order retail and cash-on-delivery business. Complete the bank customer due diligence interview, explaining the settlement flow under which local logistics partners remit cash-on-delivery proceeds to the partnership and Airwallex is used for cross-border collection. Execute the account mandate, internet banking terms, and merchant settlement agreements only after the bank has confirmed enhanced due diligence clearance. Use the approved account exclusively for COD remittances, supplier payments, customs duties, and operating expenses; maintain source-of-funds records and courier manifests in accordance with Cap 615.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Certified copy of the Business Registration Certificate
Executed first board resolution authorizing bank signatories
Executed Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed
Beneficial ownership declaration and ownership chart
AML compliance policy and procedure manual
Financial projections and cash-flow forecast for the COD e-commerce operation
Identity documents of authorized signatories and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects or queries the account application, request a written declination stating the grounds. Remedy any missing KYC documentation, simplify the ownership chain if beneficial ownership is unclear, and supplement the AML file with an external audit of source of funds. Approach another licensed bank or regulated payment institution with the corrected file; the HKMA does not guarantee approval by any particular bank but prohibits unreasonable refusal on discriminatory or improper grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-formation statutory filings and operational compliance notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and if physical parcels cross borders, Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File all post-formation declarations required by the Companies Registry, including any change of partners, change of registered office, or annual return of limited partnership particulars. Submit the Business Registration renewal and any branch registration amendments to the Inland Revenue Department before the annual renewal date. If goods are imported from mainland China or exported to emerging markets, obtain a Customs and Excise account under the Import and Export Ordinance for cargo manifest filing and e-commerce courier declarations. Confirm that no industrial operating license, Environmental Impact Assessment permit, or Civil Defense fire permit is triggered because ISIC 4791 is a pure retail and logistics-remittance operation and not a manufacturing or chemical facility. Maintain a compliance calendar showing the SLA deadlines for annual returns, Business Registration payment, Profits Tax return, customs audit, and AML internal review.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Annual return form LP3 or equivalent
Customs and Excise registration record if importing or exporting parcels
Profits Tax return filing basis and partnership profit-sharing records
AML annual review and compliance calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any annual return, Business Registration renewal, or customs declaration is filed after the statutory deadline, arrange immediate submission with a covering letter setting out reasonable cause. Apply to the relevant Registry or Department for remission or mitigation of penalties by presenting proof of posting, technical failure logs, or external solicitor delay; if penalties are nevertheless imposed, seek review through the prescribed appeal or objection procedure within the statutory objection window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial or manufacturing licensor regulates ISIC 4791 mail-order retail. If incidental physical premises are used, the relevant supplementary authorities are the Buildings Department for structural compliance and the Fire Services Department for fire safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - online mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement under ISIC 4791 does not require a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or industrial warehousing operating license. The only operational registration required is the Business Registration Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310), together with Customs registration if cross-border parcels are handled.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable for the current pure retail and fulfillment-remittance operation; the Environmental Protection Department of Hong Kong SAR would be the competent agency only if a later project triggers an industrial or large warehouse development under Schedule 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap 499).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full EIA Report, Environmental Permit, or environmental registration is required because the defined ISIC 4791 business does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, mineral extraction, or regulated warehousing activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the operation has no industrial wastewater discharge point, no regulated VOC emission source, and no hazardous waste generation. Any incidental packaging waste is governed by the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap 354) and the municipal solid waste charging scheme; the partnership shall require its logistics contractors to maintain vehicle emission compliance under the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap 311) but the partnership is not a premises-based emitter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an industrial Civil Defense fire certificate because the FIP is not an industrial, chemical, assembly, or licensed warehouse occupier under ISIC 4791. If an ancillary office, small showroom, or parcel-handling room is occupied, the partnership must comply with the Fire Safety (Commercial Premises) Ordinance (Cap 502), respond to any Fire Safety Direction issued by the Fire Services Department, and carry out a structural load and escape route assessment through a registered contractor. For staffed premises, the partnership must complete a workplace risk assessment and display safety instructions under the Occupational Safety and Occupational Health Ordinance (Cap 509).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic filing is conducted through the official STA Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) platform, with service entry via the national portal www.chinatax.gov.cn and provincial-level e-Tax portals. For Hong Kong SAR intermediate holding/financing arrangements, the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department (IRD) is the competent authority only for Hong Kong tax matters and does not issue a mainland FIP tax ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested partnership (FIP) undertaking VAT-able e-commerce activity in mainland China, the statutory procedure is: (1) the foreign partners execute the partnership agreement and appoint an authorized representative; (2) apply to the local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) for foreign-invested partnership establishment, submitting notarized or apostilled identity documents of every foreign partner, a Chinese-language translation, and the articles of partnership; (3) upon approval, the SAMR issues a Partnership Business License containing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the sole statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) for the FIP in the STA's taxpayer registry; (4) within 30 days after license issuance, the FIP must complete tax registration through the e-Tax platform of its competent STA branch, confirming the legal representative, financial officer, accounting basis, bank deposit account, VAT taxpayer status (small-scale or general VAT taxpayer), and filing period; (5) if a foreign partner is a non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in mainland China, the FIP must complete a withholding-tax registration for that non-resident partner and, where treaty relief is sought, file the treaty benefit claim with the competent STA office; the non-resident partner is then issued a non-resident taxpayer file number or covered under the FIP's withholding registration, as applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (the FIP is a tax-transparent partnership for mainland China corporate income tax purposes: the entity itself is not a CIT taxpayer and taxable income is allocated to partners under their respective resident or non-resident, corporate or individual tax regimes; China-source and non-China-source allocation follows the territorial and PE rules embedded in the partner-level tax framework).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under PRC law. China does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box entity classification election. Partnership tax transparency is mandatory under the Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration Notice on Partnership Enterprise Partner Income Tax Treatment (Cai Shui [2008] No. 159); no hybrid mismatch election is available in the PRC national regime for an FIP. Foreign partners must follow the mandatory allocations of partnership taxable income and are not permitted to elect entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (China Value-Added Tax under the PRC Provisional Regulations on Value-Added Tax and implementing rules; export zero-rating applies separately to qualifying cross-border supplies).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All licensed FIPs must complete basic tax registration immediately upon establishment regardless of turnover. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies once annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000 in any continuous 12-month rolling period; below that threshold the FIP is treated as a small-scale VAT taxpayer unless it voluntarily applies for general taxpayer status. For cross-border e-commerce mail-order retail, the zero-rated export treatment is conditional on customs clearance and export proceeds repatriation, not on the domestic turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices must be issued through STA-approved tax control and electronic invoice systems under the Golden Tax Phase IV framework. Fully digitalized electronic invoices are generated on the e-Tax platform with system-assigned invoice numbers, encrypted tax-control codes, and near-real-time invoice data transmission to the STA; the national invoice verification service is used by counterparties to confirm authenticity. Special VAT invoices are subject to the special VAT invoice tax-control device and issuance protocol and may only be issued by general taxpayers. For COD mail-order retail, an invoice must be issued when the cash is collected or the goods are delivered, whichever occurs first; each invoice must reference the underlying order, logistics receipt, and payment settlement record. There is no physical stamping requirement for fully digitalized e-invoices, but the digitally signed invoice metadata functions as the anti-fraud seal and is subject to automated risk-alert screening.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available on qualifying physical exports where the FIP is registered as an exporter with the customs authority and the STA, the goods are actually shipped out of mainland China customs territory under an export customs declaration, the buyer is located outside mainland China, and the export proceeds are repatriated through licensed banking channels and verified within the prescribed deadline. Cross-border e-commerce retail parcels may use the dedicated customs supervision mode for small-value exports (Customs Supervision Code 9610 and, where applicable, 9710 for B2B export) with a corresponding export declaration list. Qualifying digital or offshore services supplied by a Chinese-resident service provider to an overseas recipient may be zero-rated under the STA cross-border taxable services zero-rating and exemption catalogue if the service falls within the listed categories, the recipient is an overseas party, and the prescribed contract, overseas payment, and service-delivery evidence is maintained. The FIP must file the export tax refund declaration within the statutory time limit using e-Tax and customs-consolidated electronic data; failure to meet the conditions converts the supply to a domestic taxable supply at the standard VAT rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Declaration Form / Bill of Entry)
Original Bill of Lading or equivalent air waybill or courier consignment note with delivery proof
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or SAFE-compliant bank export proceeds receipt and settlement record
Export sales contract or online order agreement, including COD reconciliation report from the logistics or remittance operator (Airwallex or licensed local logistics remittance platform where used)
Logistics manifest, customs clearance record, and cross-border e-commerce export declaration list under Customs Supervision Code 9610 or 9710 where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, customs, and SAFE may jointly audit export-zero-rating claims by verifying physical cargo movement, value truthfulness, order authenticity, logistics POD, and the inward flow of foreign currency within 180 days from the export declaration date. If zero-rating is granted but the foreign-exchange repatriation or customs documentation fails verification, the exporter must repay the tax refund and the zero-rated supply is re-characterized as a domestic taxable sale at 13% VAT, with late-payment surcharge accruing at 0.05% per day from the original filing due date. Administrative penalties for false or fraudulent export tax refund claims range from 50% to 500% of the tax involved under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law; customs may also impose fines for false export declarations. Where fraud is established, the clawback is not time-barred and criminal liability for defrauding export tax refunds under the PRC Criminal Law may arise, including imprisonment and fines for responsible individuals.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) are the prudential FX authorities governing the mainland China capital account; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) oversees the Hong Kong dollar clearing and convertibility leg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China has attained current account convertibility under IMF Article VIII, but the capital account remains heavily regulated. A Foreign-Invested Partnership is treated as a resident investee for inbound FDI only after completing Foreign Investment Information Reporting and SAFE foreign exchange registration. Capital contributions remitted from Hong Kong into the FIP must be classified as capital account transactions, require an FDI capital foreign exchange account, and cannot be netted against operating expenses. Profit repatriation, capital reductions, and partner exits are subject to SAFE review, tax clearance, and documentary proof of profitability and underlying transactions. Under the mainland-Hong Kong double taxation arrangement, withholding may be reduced only after the FIP provides a Hong Kong tax residency certificate and a bank-beneficial owner declaration. In practice, remittance of profits to Hong Kong is delayed by the need to reconcile audited accounts, VAT invoices, customs declarations, and logistics proof-of-delivery records. RMB convertibility under the capital account is limited to qualified transactions; onshore RMB derived from domestic COD sales cannot be freely converted and remitted abroad without supporting trade documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts of a Chinese resident exporter, including an FIP, must be repatriated into a domestic bank account or foreign exchange settlement account within 180 days of the customs export declaration date. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio under current SAFE rules; exporters may retain foreign currency or convert into RMB, but every receipt must be matched with a customs declaration, commercial invoice, and the appropriate trade monitoring code in the SAFE foreign exchange system. For cross-border ecommerce COD transactions, proceeds remitted through licensed logistics or payment institutions must be settled into the FIP's onshore settlement account, and unsupported offshore retention or conversion is treated as a violation of surrender controls.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI foreign exchange capital account and basic operational RMB account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic operational currency account and RMB settlement account
Cross-border ecommerce settlement account with integrated logistics remittance facilities
Basic deposit account for operational payroll and domestic supplier settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex have very low direct viability as the primary onshore treasury bank for the mainland FIP. Under PRC non-bank payment institution licensing and SAFE trade monitoring rules, any platform that opens local RMB accounts, holds funds, or clears payments for a mainland enterprise must be either a licensed bank or hold a PBoC payment business permit. Airwallex is not licensed for RMB clearing in mainland China and can only serve as an ancillary overseas collection wallet for the Hong Kong parent or as a settlement layer for international ecommerce receipts outside the FIP's onshore bank accounts. Routing mainland COD proceeds through Airwallex or similar EMIs would bypass automatic FX reporting and create serious AML and SAFE violations. Therefore, the FIP must rely on PBoC-regulated domestic banks and, for permitted cross-border ecommerce, SAFE-filed licensed payment institutions rather than offshore EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for opening the mainland FIP's RMB basic account. Under PBoC settlement account rules, the legal representative or, for a partnership, at least one general partner or an authorised officer holding a notarised power of attorney must appear in person at the bank branch to complete signature verification and the KYC interview. Hong Kong signatories cannot rely solely on consular proxy or remote video onboarding; notarised and apostilled corporate documents may be used for pre-screening, but final account activation and signing of the bank's custody agreement generally require a physical branch visit or designation of a local authorised representative whose identity is verified in-branch. For the Hong Kong parent treasury account, HKMA-regulated institutions may allow a remote or proxy opening under enhanced due diligence, but the mainland FIP account remains branch-first.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership governance with passive limited partners in Hong Kong obscures ultimate beneficial ownership and the original source of capital committed to the FIP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised partnership agreement; full register of partners; beneficial ownership chart identifying every individual holding 25% or more, including corporate nominee layers; source-of-funds evidence for each partner such as three months of bank statements, securities liquidation slips, or certified sale contracts; notarised passports or Hong Kong company certificates; and for corporate partners, a Certificate of Incumbency with shareholder register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-value cash-on-delivery collections arrive from logistics couriers or remittance companies, creating transaction patterns inconsistent with declared revenue and suggesting possible layering or underreporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit daily COD cash and electronic settlement ledgers from every logistics partner; platform payout reports; proof-of-delivery logs; refund and chargeback registers; signed service agreements with logistics providers; and management reports reconciling courier remittances with underlying online orders, plus an independent accountancy firm audit trail over COD revenue recognition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound remittance from the Hong Kong parent is coded as a trade payment or ordinary current account transfer instead of a capital injection, or arrives before SAFE FDI registration has been completed, generating a false purpose flag and possible round-tripping exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the Foreign Investment Information Reporting receipt; SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration certificate with bank seal; SWIFT MT103 containing the stated capital injection purpose and FDI registration reference; partner subscription and payment schedules; and a capital verification report issued by a licensed PRC certified public accountant after funds are received in the designated capital account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person screening reveals that a partner or beneficial owner shares names or citizenship with an individual in a restricted jurisdiction, or negative regulatory news is detected around the Hong Kong shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide independent SDN, EU, UN and PRC sanctioned-list screening results; negative news search with source links; PEP declaration; six months of bank statements for the relevant partner showing licit source of wealth; Hong Kong tax clearance certificates; and a written PRC/HK legal opinion confirming beneficial ownership, eligibility, and economic substance of the FIP transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before funding, the FIP must be registered with SAMR and complete the Foreign Investment Information Report, followed by SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration through a designated bank. The FIP then opens a basic RMB account and a separate FDI capital foreign exchange account. The Hong Kong investor remits via SWIFT MT103 or CHATS in USD or HKD to the receiving bank, stating the purpose as direct investment capital contribution and quoting the SAFE FDI registration number. The receiving PRC bank performs KYC, checks the capital account-credit against the FDI registration slip, applies the onshore spot rate if conversion into RMB is elected, and credits the capital account. A Chinese CPA then issues an inward capital verification report. Any subsequent increase in registered capital must be re-registered with SAFE and SAMR before disbursement; using personal accounts, e-wallets, or unlicensed EMI rails for capital injection is non-compliant and will trigger holdbacks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade and operating payments, the FIP should prioritise CIPS for RMB-denominated settlements and SWIFT MT103 for USD or HKD payables, accompanied by a SAFE trade purpose declaration and underlying contract and customs documents. High-value inventory procurement from overseas can be settled through an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit opened by the FIP's mainland bank and advised by a Hong Kong confirming bank, enhancing payment security and financing capacity. For established suppliers, Documentary Collections under Documents against Payment or Documents against Acceptance provide a lower-cost clearing rail but require disciplined document checking and customs coordination. Domestic COD proceeds should be swept daily from logistics partners into the operational bank account, while international ecommerce receivables should be routed through SAFE-recorded licensed payment institutions before settlement into the onshore account; all rails must leave complete reconciliation evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts in USD/CNY and HKD/CNY, available only for genuine trade or capital exposure and executed through a domestic settlement bank with SAFE-registered derivative authorisation
Cross-currency swaps on the currency and interest rate legs of a long-term capital obligation or acquisition loan, subject to SAFE approval and documentary proof of the underlying hedge exposure
Onshore currency options for hedging trade receivables and payables, with option premiums paid from the FIP's operational account and subject to bank product eligibility

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted as onshore FIP instruments; the Hong Kong parent treasury may use NDFs only for the offshore HKD leg, and such positions must never be booked or funded from the mainland FIP account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the expiry date of the current certificate; for a 1-year certificate, renewal is due within 1 month after expiry if not paid in advance during the 3-month renewal window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late renewal fee of HKD 300 per month (maximum HKD 3,000) plus a penalty of HKD 5,000 applies; continued non-renewal triggers cancellation of the business registration and criminal prosecution with fines up to HKD 10,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnership (Form BIR52)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 3 months after the date of issue, with the IRD ordinarily issuing returns on 1 April; electronic filing via a tax representative may extend the deadline to 15 August
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of up to HKD 10,000, and an additional penalty may be imposed of up to 300% of unpaid tax under Section 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance; habitual non-filing may result in a forced assessment and legal action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month after 31 March each year, covering the preceding fiscal year (1 April to 31 March); if electronically filed with a tax representative, the deadline may extend to 15 August
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is liable to a fine of HKD 12,000 and imprisonment for 3 months; repeated offences attract a HKD 25,000 fine and a daily default penalty of HKD 100

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Confirmation and Change Notices (if structured as LP/LPF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in general or limited partner particulars (including shareholdings, contributions, or registered address); a written annual confirmation must be delivered on each anniversary of registration if no changes have occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the required notice or annual confirmation renders the partnership liable to a fine of HKD 50,000 and a continuing fine of HKD 50 per day; any partner responsible may also be prosecuted

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Foreign-Invested Partnership structured as a limited partnership must undergo a mandatory independent CPA audit if, in any financial year, it meets any two of the following quantitative thresholds: (1) total annual revenue exceeding HKD 10 million (~USD 1.28 million); (2) total assets exceeding HKD 10 million (~USD 1.28 million); or (3) average number of employees exceeding 50. Additionally, the Inland Revenue Ordinance (section 51C) and relevant IRD practice require audited financial statements to be attached to the Profits Tax Return when gross turnover exceeds HKD 5 million (~USD 641,000) or where the partnership has previously been selected for audit by the IRD. A statutory audit is also compulsory if the partnership engages in a regulated activity under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap 571) or operates as a licensed standalone fund entity under the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), which are fully converged with IFRS; small private entities may apply the Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standard for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE), a simplified framework, if they satisfy the statutory small-entity criteria under the Companies Ordinance

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Hong Kong law, an FIP structured as a limited partnership is not subject to the public Significant Controllers Register (SCR) regime applicable to private companies. Instead, the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37) and the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance (Cap 637) require the partnership to maintain a contemporaneous register of all general and limited partners, including details of capital contributions and ownership percentages. Any change in partner particulars or shareholding transfers must be reported to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the change. For anti-money laundering compliance, the partnership must adopt a risk-based approach and conduct annual UBO due diligence, but there is no annual public UBO filing requirement. If the partnership operates as a Limited Partnership Fund, the responsible persons must deliver an annual confirmation to the Companies Registry that the partnership continues to comply with the terms of the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The FIP itself is tax-transparent; no CIT is assessed at partnership level. Resident corporate partners apply the 25% headline rate, with reductions for qualified small low-profit enterprises (annual taxable income <= CNY 3 million, total assets <= CNY 50 million, employees <= 300) to an effective 5% CIT rate; certain encouraged industries in Western China and the Hainan Free Trade Port may access a 15% rate; qualifying R&D expenses receive a 100% additional deduction; and qualifying technology transfer income is exempt up to CNY 5 million with 50% tax inclusion on the excess. Non-resident partners without a PRC permanent establishment are subject to final gross-basis withholding, not the 25% net-basis rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return of the People's Republic of China (Form A100000), together with Schedule B100000 (Partnership Income Allocation) and the Non-Resident Enterprise Withholding Income Tax Return, all filed through the State Taxation Administration National E-Tax Portal. Because the Foreign-Invested Partnership is pass-through, each corporate partner files its own CIT return; non-resident partners report China-source allocations through the withholding agent's return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement filing, with quarterly provisional CIT filings for PRC-resident corporate partners and withholding returns at each profit distribution or payment date for non-resident partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end; quarterly provisional CIT filings are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; non-resident withholding returns are due on the day of distribution or within 15 days thereafter as prescribed by the withholding obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Operating Revenue from all goods sold, including cross-border mail-order and cash-on-delivery e-commerce transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross revenue on the settlement date when the logistics provider or payment-service provider remits the COD collection to the FIP. Revenue must not be netted against Airwallex payment fees, remittance charges, or delivery commissions. For a non-resident partner with no permanent establishment in the PRC, only passive profit allocations are reported; however, if the FIP concludes contracts, warehouses goods, or exercises contract-negotiating authority in China, the non-resident partner may be deemed to have a permanent establishment and must shift from gross-basis withholding to net-basis CIT under Article 5 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

Deduct property documented cost of goods sold, inventory costs, freight, customs duties, platform fees, payment-processing fees, and cash-collection agency fees. Expenses involving related parties must be arm's length and supported by valid fapiao-equivalent vouchers; otherwise the tax authority will recharacterize or disallow them. A non-resident partner's foreign overhead cannot be deducted against China-source gross income; only expenses directly attributable to a PRC permanent establishment are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Profit / Partnership Allocable Book Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile this line to audited financial statements and the partnership income allocation schedule. The FIP must show each partner's allocable share of China-source and foreign-source income. Non-resident partners must not offset foreign operating losses against China-source profit. All COD deposits collected by logistics agents must be deposited promptly into the FIP bank account; any mismatch between cash collections and reported revenue is a serious audit red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustments: Transfer Pricing, Thin Capitalization and Non-Taxable Items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter positive adjustments for non-arm's-length related-party transactions, disallowed related-party interest in excess of the 2:1 debt/equity ratio, non-commercial intra-group service charges, and royalties paid to a no-substance IP owner. A non-resident partner must prove, through contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, that every cross-border recharge and payment is priced at arm's length; otherwise the tax authority may impute profit and impose penalties under Articles 41 and 121 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

Only a PRC-resident corporate partner may carry forward its allocable share of FIP tax losses for a maximum of 5 years, except that qualifying high-technology small and medium enterprises may use a 10-year carryforward. Losses allocated to a non-resident partner without a PRC permanent establishment cannot offset China-source passive income subject to withholding. A change in partnership ownership may trigger a loss-utilization ceiling recalculation under Article 18 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income and Tax Payable at Partner Level
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident corporate partners compute taxable income at 25% or any applicable reduced rate. If a non-resident partner is deemed to have a permanent establishment, its allocable profit after permitted adjustments is taxed at 25% and foreign tax credits may apply. If no permanent establishment exists, these corporate CIT boxes are left at zero and the distribution is instead reported on the Non-Resident Enterprise Withholding Income Tax Return at the statutory 10% gross rate, subject to treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, Foreign Tax Credits and Final Balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset quarterly provisional CIT paid by resident partners and claim foreign tax credits only with valid foreign tax residency certificates and underlying assessment documents. A non-resident Hong Kong partner may claim the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement foreign tax credit against Hong Kong profits tax on the same income; refund claims must be made within three years under the Tax Collection Administration Law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing exposes the taxpayer to a fine of RMB 2,000-10,000 under Article 62 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, rising to RMB 10,000-50,000 in serious cases. Late payment attracts daily interest of 0.05% on the unpaid tax. A false or incomplete return that causes underpayment is punishable under Article 63 with a fine equal to 50%-500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law can lead to imprisonment of up to 7 years, criminal fines, asset confiscation, tax authority blacklisting, exit bans, and disqualification of responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% gross withholding under Articles 3(3) and 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law on profit distributions or partnership allocations to a non-resident partner without a PRC permanent establishment; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement only for a beneficial owner that is a Hong Kong tax resident company holding at least 25% of the entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the DTA relief, the withholding agent must obtain from the non-resident partner before or on the withholding return date: (i) a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department, (ii) a beneficial ownership declaration supported by substance evidence such as office premises, local staff, board minutes, and business decision-making records, and (iii) a completed treaty claim statement filed with the PRC tax authority. The claim must be renewed annually. If the tax authority later denies treaty benefits, the FIP or withholding agent must pay the differential 10% gross withholding plus late-payment interest and may face a 50% penalty for a false beneficial-ownership claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory PRC withholding rate for outbound royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10%. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement, interest and royalties beneficially owned by Hong Kong residents are generally capped at 7%. Service fees that are not royalties remain subject to VAT, corporate income tax, and transfer pricing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation becomes mandatory for an FIP/corporate partner when annual related-party tangible property transfers exceed CNY 200 million, intangible property transfers exceed CNY 20 million, controlled financing transactions exceed CNY 40 million, controlled service transactions exceed CNY 40 million, or aggregate group controlled transactions exceed CNY 1 billion triggering Master File preparation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC does not have a separate cross-the-board Economic Substance Regulations statute, but economic substance is enforced through the beneficial ownership rule for DTA claims, the Controlled Foreign Corporation rule under Article 45 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, and the General Anti-Abuse Rule under Article 47. For Hong Kong corporate partners, the Hong Kong foreign-source income exemption rules require that core income-generating activities with respect to offshore passive income be performed in Hong Kong. The FIP must demonstrate that COD logistics, payment settlement, inventory risk, and contract acceptance take place in China; without substance, the tax authority may recharacterize the arrangement and pierce the corporate/partnership form for tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP instructs the logistics provider to collect COD cash from consumers and deposit it into an offshore bank account held by a non-resident partner instead of the FIP's PRC bank account; no revenue is recorded on the CIT return and no partnership income allocation schedule is filed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 6 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law all income must be included; under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law the taxpayer is liable to a fine equal to 50%-500% of the underpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest of 0.05%; criminal Article 201 of the Criminal Law applies with imprisonment up to 7 years and criminal fines for intentional concealment of taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and directors who order or approve the side-settlement are jointly and severally liable for the underpaid tax and penalties under partnership unlimited-liability principles; their personal assets may be subject to civil restitution and clawback; the tax authority blacklists them and imposes travel bans, and responsible officers face criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-Company Treaty Abuse / Fake Hong Kong Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Hong Kong corporate partner with no premises, staff, or decision-making function holds an interest in the FIP solely to obtain the 5% DTA withholding rate on outbound profit distributions, while actual management of logistics, cash collection, and payment remittance is performed from mainland China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DTA benefits are denied under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and OECD BEPS Action 6; the differential withholding is raised to the statutory 10% rate with 0.05% daily interest and a false-claim penalty under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law of 50%-500%; Hong Kong Inland Revenue may also impose penalties for inconsistent non-establishment declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial-ownership certificates and treaty claim statements are personally liable for the tax shortfall; both PRC and Hong Kong authorities may impose travel restrictions and blacklisting; where the conduit arrangement conceals taxable income, directors face criminal liability for aiding tax evasion or fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP uses Airwallex and local logistics remittance corridors to collect and split consumer cash-like COD payments without performing adequate customer due diligence or filing suspicious transaction reports, and structures daily settlement batches below regulatory thresholds to avoid review; the funds are then used for related-party disbursements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law, the entity may be fined up to RMB 5,000,000 and directly responsible persons up to RMB 500,000, with suspension of business and license revocation; under Criminal Law Article 191, money laundering carries imprisonment of 5-10 years, criminal fines, and confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are personally liable for civil restitution and are subject to asset clawback; travel bans and tax/AML blacklisting apply upon sanction; criminal liability attaches where directors knowingly structure cash flows to avoid regulatory scrutiny, allowing the court to pierce the corporate veil and impose imprisonment and personal fines.
